subject: Private Offer Listing — Contoso: commercial amendment & billing path
messages:
From: Contoso Procurement <procurement@contoso.com>
To: Markus Klein <markus_klein@redwood.ai>
Cc: Azure Marketplace PM <marketplace@microsoft.com>, Rachel Zhou <rachel.zhou@contoso.com>
Date: Sun, 3 May 2026 14:22:00 -0700
Subject: Contoso private plan listing — commercial questions

Hi Markus,

Thanks for the call last week — Contoso is ready to move forward with an Azure private offer for the pilot. Before we proceed we need to lock a few commercial items so our procurement and legal teams can issue a PO:

- Confirm Redwood's acceptance of Contoso's standard PO (we will provide terms).
- Confirm billing path: Contoso prefers Azure commerce billing (Microsoft) rather than direct billing. Is that supported for your private plans?
- Revenue share / co-sell exhibit: we need to understand if any revenue-share/partner commission is required for co-sell registration.
- Liability/indemnity: Contoso has a standard indemnity cap tied to contract value — will Redwood accept a cap at 1x contract value?

Please send the most recent amendment you put together for Azure private offers and a short checklist of next steps so procurement knows timing. We have a PO ready to attach once language is agreed.

Regards,
Procurement Team
Contoso Corporation
attachments: none
From: Markus Klein <markus_klein@redwood.ai>
To: Contoso Procurement <procurement@contoso.com>
Cc: Laura Bennett <laura_bennett@redwood.ai>, Azure Marketplace PM <marketplace@microsoft.com>, Priyom Das <priyom_das@redwood.ai>
Date: Mon, 4 May 2026 09:12:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Contoso private plan listing — commercial questions

Hi Rachel / Contoso procurement,

Thanks — great to hear Contoso is ready. Attached is our working draft amendment for Azure private offers that covers billing, acceptance, and marketplace-specific exhibits (Redwood_Azure_Private_Plan_Amendment_v2.docx). High level on your bullets: 

- PO acceptance: yes, we can accept a Contoso-issued PO but need the PO to reference the final amendment and SOW.
- Billing path: we can route billing via Azure commerce for private offers; it requires an "Azure commerce" exhibit and mapping of SKUs. There are a couple operational items (invoice routing, reconciliation window) that the marketplace PM will need to confirm.
- Revenue share: Redwood does not require a partner carve for co-sell registration; the marketplace rules vary by program — we can adopt whichever co-sell exhibit Microsoft requires and reflect it in the amendment.
- Indemnity cap: our standard position is 1x contract value but we prefer carve-outs for IP infringement and breach-related damages. Laura, can you confirm if we can accept Contoso's 1x cap with the listed carve-outs?

Next steps I propose:
1) Laura to provide redlines to the attached amendment.
2) Contoso to send PO + any redlines.
3) Marketplace PM to confirm technical steps for private offer publish and billing manifest.
4) Execute via DocuSign.

Can we target a signed amendment by Friday next week if all parties align?

Best,
Markus Klein
Head of Partnerships, Redwood Inference
attachments: Redwood_Azure_Private_Plan_Amendment_v2.docx
From: Laura Bennett <laura_bennett@redwood.ai>
To: Markus Klein <markus_klein@redwood.ai>, Priyom Das <priyom_das@redwood.ai>, Contoso Procurement <procurement@contoso.com>
Cc: Azure Marketplace PM <marketplace@microsoft.com>
Date: Tue, 5 May 2026 11:03:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Contoso private plan listing — commercial questions

Markus / team / Rachel,

Thanks — I'm attaching a redlined version with comments (Redwood_Azure_Private_Plan_Amendment_v3.docx). Key legal positions and alternatives:

1) Indemnity cap: we can accept a 1x contract value cap as proposed, provided we carve out (a) IP infringement indemnities and (b) breach of confidentiality/data protection claims. If Contoso insists on no carve-outs, we will need to reduce exposure elsewhere (e.g., shorter warranty window).

2) Data handling & retention: Contoso has a stricter retention schedule in its template. We propose referencing our Customer Data Processing Addendum and limiting retention periods tied to the pilot timeline.

3) Billing via Azure commerce: operationally fine, but we need a short manifest clause stating that Microsoft is the billing agent and that Redwood's obligation to invoice is satisfied by the Azure commerce invoice. This prevents duplicate billing claims.

4) Audit rights: Contoso's audit window is 5 years in their PO. We propose a 2-year window for billing-related audits and an obligation to use reasonable, non-disruptive audit procedures.

If Contoso's team can confirm acceptance of the carve-outs above, I can sign off and we can push the DocuSign envelope. Otherwise, we'll need one round of back-and-forth on redlines.

Laura Bennett
Senior Counsel, Redwood Inference
attachments: Redwood_Azure_Private_Plan_Amendment_v3.docx
From: Rachel Zhou <rachel.zhou@contoso.com>
To: Markus Klein <markus_klein@redwood.ai>, Laura Bennett <laura_bennett@redwood.ai>, Priyom Das <priyom_das@redwood.ai>
Cc: Contoso Procurement <procurement@contoso.com>, Azure Marketplace PM <marketplace@microsoft.com>
Date: Thu, 7 May 2026 08:30:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Contoso private plan listing — commercial questions

Hi all,

Thanks for the redlines, Laura — that helps clarify. Procurement reviewed and here's where Contoso lands: 

- Indemnity cap: Contoso will accept the 1x contract value cap with the proposed carve-outs for IP infringement and data breach, provided Redwood confirms those carve-outs are tracked in the amendment.
- Billing: Contoso requires Azure commerce billing. Azure marketplace PM has indicated this is supported for our subscription model; Contoso expects Microsoft to issue invoice and Contoso will pay Microsoft. Contoso asks Redwood to confirm the manifest clause language and that Redwood will not separately invoice Contoso for the same invoice period.
- Audit window: Contoso will reduce to a 3-year billing audit window as a compromise.

Attached are Contoso's redlines and the PO — Contoso_PO_7892.pdf and Contoso_Redlines.pdf. We are ready to sign once the amendment reflects the carve-outs and the billing manifest language.

Next: Please confirm you will update the amendment and initiate DocuSign.

Thanks,
Rachel
Procurement Manager, Contoso

Rachel — great, thanks for the quick turnaround and for attaching the PO.

We accept the compromise as summarized: 1x indemnity cap with the two carve-outs, 3-year audit window for billing, and Azure commerce billing with a manifest clause confirming Microsoft as the billing agent. Laura will incorporate the manifest language and final clauses; I will kick off DocuSign once the amendment is updated.

Operational notes:

- Contoso: once DocuSign is sent, please sign the amendment and then upload the PO to the DocuSign envelope (or email to contracts@redwood.ai).

I'll send the envelope today: https://www.docusign.com/envelope/ABC123456789 (DocuSign) — Azure Private Offer ID will be 38-REDWOOD-PRV-2026 once published.

Thanks,
